page: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 35 MB of Level 3 cache and supports vector extensions including AVX-512 and VNNI. Providing 256 GB of system RAM, the instance establishes a 16 GB per vCPU memory allocation. It carries no local ephemeral storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, depending entirely on external premium managed disks for persistent storage needs.

Benchmark evaluations position the computational and memory capabilities of the server within the median range of comparable cloud instances. It registered a multi-core Stress-ng score of 14,909.58, a PassMark CPU score of 15,961.04, and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8,028.0. In memory throughput testing, uncached memory bandwidth reached 85.20 GB/sec for sequential reads and 46.97 GB/sec for writes. The platform demonstrated notable throughput in key-value testing, achieving 14.09 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations metric of 5,801.91. Conversely, heavier generative workloads highlight architectural limits, with medium 7B parameter LLM prompt processing scoring in the lower quartile at 24.28 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators.

The constrained vCPU allocation of the E32-16s_v4 yields distinct architectural and licensing efficiencies, providing the 256 GB memory footprint of an equivalent 32-core VM while maintaining only 16 active vCPUs. This configuration reduces per-core software licensing expenditures without degrading memory density. A key tradeoff remains the absence of onboard NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies fully on attached network block storage. The instance fits memory-heavy applications that do not require proportional CPU scaling, such as Redis caching clusters, large relational database engines, and in-memory analytical workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, accompanied by 256 GB of RAM. Designed with a constrained CPU-to-memory ratio of 16 GB per vCPU, this instance optimizes memory density while lowering core-count licensing requirements. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and VNNI extensions. Benchmarks place raw processing and memory bandwidth in the median tier, demonstrated by 85.20 GB/sec large-block read speeds, 14.09 million Redis SET operations per second, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,028.0. The instance lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and offers weak throughput on heavier LLM prompt processing without GPU accelerators. The E32-16s_v4 is well adapted for in-memory caching systems, large relational database engines, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
